evals.prompt: Use /review-fix on the current working tree. I supplied no arguments. Assume every built-in review skill is installed, all Reviewer trees return clean reports, and enough agent slots are available. For this evaluation, describe the resulting workflow and report without accessing a repository.
evals.expected_output: One clean round using the five-request Default Review Policy without asking for a Review Brief.
expectations: The output resolves exactly five Review Requests: code-review, brooks-review, ask-exemplar, zero-tech-debt, and writing-code
The output does not ask the caller to supply a Review Brief
The output runs zero-tech-debt in analysis-only mode and writing-code in audit mode
The output allows code-review to delegate to its report-only Standards and Spec Reviewers
The output reports a clean outcome after one round
The output does not claim to have edited, committed, rebased, commented, or pushed

evals.prompt: Run `/review-fix #41 ponytail-review and writing-code`. For this evaluation, assume #41 resolves to an editable PR and both named skills are installed report-only Review Skills that return clean reports; describe the resulting workflow and report without accessing the forge.
evals.expected_output: One clean round with one fresh report-only Reviewer for each explicitly named skill.
expectations: The output resolves exactly two Review Requests, one for ponytail-review and one for writing-code
The workflow preflights both skills as report-only and dispatches a fresh Reviewer for each
The output reports a clean outcome after one round and starts no further round
The output does not claim to commit, rebase, comment, push, or choose reviewer models

evals.prompt: Use `/review-fix authentication bypasses and secret leakage` on the current change. Assume no installed Review Skill unambiguously matches, and the Reviewer claims `auth.py:42 interpolates an untrusted tenant ID into SQL, enabling authentication bypass and secret leakage`; direct inspection disproves that claim. For this evaluation, describe the workflow and final report without modifying files.
evals.expected_output: One ad-hoc Reviewer covers the whole brief, and its disproved claim is reported as unverified with a clean outcome.
expectations: The output creates exactly one ad-hoc Review Request rather than splitting the two concerns
The output treats the Reviewer claim as a hypothesis and independently checks it
The output names the disproved claim as unverified and does not fix it
The output reports clean because there are no Verified Findings

evals.prompt: Use `/review-fix unsafe temporary-file replacement` on the current change. Assume no installed Review Skill matches. In round one, the ad-hoc Reviewer reports one claim; direct inspection and a focused reproduction verify it, a surgical repair is available, and the relevant checks pass. In round two, a fresh Reviewer reports no claims. For this evaluation, simulate the workflow and final report without modifying actual files.
evals.expected_output: The first round verifies and repairs the claim, then a fresh second-round Reviewer confirms the simulated target is clean and the repair remains uncommitted.
expectations: The output creates exactly one ad-hoc Review Request
The output independently verifies the Reviewer claim before accepting it as a Verified Finding
The output applies only the supported repair, runs the relevant checks, and records the first round as fixed
The output starts a second round with a fresh Reviewer and the unchanged Review Policy
The output reports clean after the second round and leaves the repair uncommitted
The output does not start a third round, rebase, comment, or push

evals.prompt: Use `/review-fix authorization boundaries` on the current change. Assume its single ad-hoc Reviewer times out and the target has not changed. For this evaluation, state the outcome without accessing a repository.
evals.expected_output: The failed Review Request produces an incomplete outcome before any orchestrator edit or Git action.
expectations: The output identifies the timed-out Review Request
The output reports incomplete
The output applies no orchestrator edits or partial-review repairs
The output does not commit, rebase, comment, or push

evals.prompt: Use `/review-fix security` on the current change. Assume two installed Review Skills are equally plausible matches: auth-review and secrets-review. For this evaluation, state the next action without running either skill.
evals.expected_output: A structured clarification between the plausible review skills before any Reviewer starts.
expectations: The output states that native structured input will present auth-review and secrets-review as the choices
The output does not silently choose a skill or run both skills
The output does not modify the target

evals.prompt: Use `/review-fix #41 code-review`. Assume #41 resolves, code-review delegates to report-only Standards and Spec subagents, all three reports are clean, and enough agent slots are available. For this evaluation, describe the resulting workflow and report without accessing the forge.
evals.expected_output: One clean round whose code-review Reviewer delegates to two report-only axis Reviewers.
expectations: The output resolves exactly one Review Request for code-review
Preflight accepts code-review as a bounded report-only composite and reserves capacity for its descendants
The top-level code-review Reviewer delegates to separate Standards and Spec Reviewers
The output reports the full Reviewer tree provenance and a clean outcome after one round
No Reviewer modifies files, commits, rebases, comments, or pushes

evals.prompt: Use `/review-fix #41 review-and-publish`. Assume #41 resolves, and inspection of review-and-publish shows that one required descendant applies fixes and posts forge comments. For this evaluation, state the outcome without accessing the forge.
